equity_bridge.item: Carrier-shareholder receivables stretch beyond steady state, FY2026-FY2028 (PV at 6.5%)
equity_bridge.note: The FY2026 year-1 flow assumes the H1 FY2026 accrual FCF (~RMB9.5bn, uncollected at 30 June: OCF 7,135 vs EBITDA-tax 27,107) is collected within the year, and the June net debt already absorbed the H1 cash drain. Base judgment: FY2026 build of RMB14bn (H1 accrual not collected + ~5bn further H2 stretch), FY2027 +8bn, FY2028 +4bn, then stable relative to revenue (handled by wc_capture_pct). PV = 14/1.065 + 8/1.065^2 + 4/1.065^3 = 23.5bn = RMB1.34/share = HK$1.56/share. The bridge is scenario-invariant; bull normalisation (an unwind of the ~RMB60bn excess over contractual terms would be worth ~HK$4/share) and bear persistence are carried in the scenario margin paths and caps, and stated in the narratives. Source: H1 FY2026 interim note 14(b), MD&A 'Capital expenditures and cash flow'.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Long-run judgment anchored on the equity 5-yr CAGR (1.8%) and management's 'steady development' framing of the TSP business: tower revenue is flat-to-shrinking (-0.3% FY2025, -6.7% H1 FY2026), Two Wings (+12-17%) is only 16% of revenue. Terminal growth 1.5% base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (4.4%) and EPS (12.6%) 5-yr CAGRs. EPS growth is a depreciation-schedule effect (D&A falling as 2015-injected towers are fully depreciated: 50.2bn FY2024 -> 48.5bn FY2025 -> 19.1bn H1 FY2026) and a 77% payout, not operating leverage; EBITDA fell in FY2025 (-1.1%) and H1 FY2026 (-11.6%).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - full lease payments; SBC zero, interest income not stripped): FY2020 10,519 -> FY2022 26,336 -> FY2025 15,091 (RMB m). The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR of -16.9% vs reported -11.1% shows lease payments growing (9.0bn -> 10.5bn) while cash conversion deteriorated; the receivables build (see inputs.receivables_note) is the dominant driver of the FY2023-25 swing, not operations.

scenario_narratives.base: A policy-mandated monopoly annuity that is ex-growth: tower leasing (75% of revenue) shrinks 1-2%/yr as 5G build-out matures and site-fee savings are passed through, DAS and the Two Wings (16% of revenue, +12-17%) roughly offset, and the FY2028 pricing-agreement renewal with the three carrier-shareholders costs ~2% of revenue. EBITDA margin settles at 60.5% (post-IFRS-16, lease charge 9.8% taken separately); D&A ex-ROU and capex converge at 24-25% of revenue as the 2015-injected towers finish depreciating. Accrual owner FCF ~RMB19-20bn/yr; the carriers' payment stretch continues through FY2028 (RMB23.5bn PV deducted in the bridge) then stabilises, so the retained cash beyond the 77%-payout dividend goes to debt reduction rather than further receivables. Terminal 14x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2028 renewal is price-neutral, 5G-A/'Six Networks' densification and a rising tenancy ratio hold tower revenue flat, DAS and Two Wings compound to 2.5% group growth, margins recover to 63.5% as bad-debt provisioning normalises and site-cost savings are retained, and -- the axis that matters most -- the carrier-shareholders bring payment terms back toward contract, unwinding part of the ~RMB60bn excess receivable. That unwind (~HK$4/share if complete) is NOT in this scenario's number; the bull value reflects only growth, margin and a 16x cap, so it is conservative on that axis.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tower revenue keeps falling at the H1 FY2026 rate (-6.7%) as Telecom/Unicom network sharing removes sites, the FY2028 renewal cuts tariffs outright as the 2015/2018 cycles did, and the carrier-shareholders treat China Tower as a financing source indefinitely: receivables keep stretching and bad debts rise, modelled as a permanent 3pt EBITDA-margin leakage on top of a 2pt tariff/mix hit (55% margin), with capex held at 26% because build-out is state-directed. Terminal 11x. This is close to a dividend-only valuation (DDM memo HK$6.8-7.7).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the contracted tower annuity as an unlevered owner-FCF stream in RMB at a 6.5% WACC (9% CoE, 36% cheap SOE debt), with leases as an operating cost, SBC zero, a 10-year explicit path that carries the FY2028 pricing reset and the D&A/capex re-basing, and a 14x terminal cap that refuses the Gordon 20x an ex-growth annuity with captive-but-controlling customers has not earned. The accrual-versus-cash gap is charged explicitly: a RMB23.5bn bridge deduction for the FY2026-28 receivables stretch, -60% working-capital capture on growth, and a bear scenario in which the leakage is permanent. Cross-check: a dividend discount model on the FY2025 DPS of RMB0.45789 (77% payout, 'steady growth' guidance) at the 9% cost of equity gives HK$6.8 at 1% growth and HK$7.7 at 2%; the gap between that and the base DCF is the value of the ~RMB12bn/yr of retained accrual FCF actually reaching shareholders (as debt paydown or higher payout) rather than financing the carriers. The market price sits between the DDM and the DCF base, which is where it should sit if the receivables question is open.
key_risks_to_valuation: Receivables stretch persists or worsens: every further RMB10bn of uncollected carrier receivables is ~HK$0.67/share of value transferred to the controlling shareholders; the base bridge assumes it stops growing after FY2028.
FY2028 Commercial Pricing Agreement renewal: base assumes -2% of revenue; a 15%->10%-style markup cut on tower tariffs would be closer to the bear's -5% and ~HK$1.5/share.
Terminal multiple: the cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 6.5%/1.5% is 20x). Each 1x on the 14x base cap is ~HK$0.65/share.

WACC: a 9% CoE on 1.8% CGBs embeds a 2.3pt SOE/H-share premium; a pure-CAPM 5.5% WACC would lift the base only modestly because the cap binds, but a 8% WACC (if cheap SOE debt is not sustainable) takes ~HK$1.2/share off.

D&A and tax: EPS growth is a depreciation-schedule effect; as D&A ex-ROU falls from 37% to 24% of revenue, cash tax rises ~RMB3bn/yr, which the component build already charges -- a model that carried FY2025 FCF margin forward would overstate value.
RMB/HKD: all value is RMB; a 5% RMB depreciation is a 5% cut in HKD IV; refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate (1.1721 at 2026-10-10).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 8.65-12.85. CNY/HKD from Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10.
data_sources.financials: 0788.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, RMB millions, FY2017-FY2025 + H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026) and kpis (LeasePayments, Depreciation, CashTaxesPaid, InterestIncome, FinanceCosts). Balance sheet, receivables aging/customer split, lease payments and ROU depreciation from 0788.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (notes 11, 13, 14, 17, 18) and 0788.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (notes 16, 19, 22, 23).
data_sources.qualitative: 0788.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-11): business model, 2023-27 Commercial Pricing Agreement, Two Wings strategy, segment growth rates, guidance and sell-side context (CMBI HK$12.1, UBS HK$11.6 DDM).

inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: the 2019 Restricted Share Incentive Scheme is dormant -- all grants were forfeited in 2022 and no active scheme exists (H1 FY2026 interim note 11 and note 17(c)); the 119.6m trust-held shares are already inside the issued count. Explicit SBC rows kept at 0%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. CNY/HKD 1.1721 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-10 (model -> quote: multiply RMB per-share values by 1.1721). No dual listing exists for a parity check (H-shares only); cross-check: FY2025 DPS RMB0.45789 x 1.1721 = HK$0.537, consistent with the HK$-denominated dividend the company actually remitted (yield ~5.8% at inputs.price_as_of).
inputs.price_note: HKEX regular close, Friday 9 October 2026; not an after-hours print. 52-week range 8.65-12.85.
inputs.share_count_basis: 17,600.85m shares in issue post the 10-for-1 consolidation of 2025-02-20 (share capital RMB17,600,847,102, par RMB1). No dilutive potential ordinary shares (FY2025 AR note: none for the years presented). Held FLAT: SBC is zero and there is no non-SBC issuance planned.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Borrowings only, at 30 June 2026: current RMB60,352m + non-current RMB17,402m = RMB77,754m, less cash RMB6,655m = RMB71,099m. Lease liabilities (RMB16,630m + 7,008m = 23,638m) are EXCLUDED because the full lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The company's own 'net debt' of RMB94,737m includes the leases; the two are consistent once the lease charge is in the flows. Interest paid on borrowings (RMB1,445m FY2025) is classified in financing, so reported OCF is pre-interest and the flows are unlevered.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency. Cost of equity 9.0%: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~0.75 (contracted infrastructure annuity) x China ERP ~6.5% gives a CAPM ~6.7%; the house carries the same 9.0% CoE as the sibling SOE telecoms 0728.HK and 0762.HK for state-owned-enterprise governance and H-share minority status, applied identically to all three scenarios. Pre-tax cost of debt ~2.1% (FY2025 interest paid RMB1,445m on ~RMB68bn average borrowings; LPR-linked SOE bank loans and MTNs), 1.6% after 25% tax. Capital weights at inputs.price_as_of: equity RMB138bn (17,601m x HK$9.185 / 1.1721) vs borrowings RMB77.8bn -> E 64% / D 36%. WACC = 0.64 x 9.0% + 0.36 x 1.6% = 6.3%, rounded to 6.5%. Customer-concentration, pricing-renewal and receivables risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal and interest, one cash-flow line: RMB10,506m FY2025, RMB4,669m H1 FY2026, 'Payments of lease liabilities (including principal and interest)') is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (~9.8% of revenue), lease liabilities are excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: 48,454 - 10,965 ROU = 37,489m, 37.3% of revenue; H1 FY2026: 19,141 - 5,409 = 13,732m, 28.2% annualised) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line. Site ground leases are a perpetual operating cost of a tower business and the lease liability covers only ~2.2 years of payments, so treating leases as debt would understate the cost materially.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are RMB2m of equity and RMB1m of profit -- immaterial, ignored. Flows are effectively 100% attributable.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income is RMB36m/yr on a net-debt balance sheet; not stripped and no cash pile is in the bridge (nothing to double-count).
inputs.receivables_note: The central cash-conversion problem. Trade and other receivables: RMB42.3bn (FY2022) -> 71.7bn (FY2023) -> 85.9bn (FY2024) -> 88.5bn (FY2025) -> 110.7bn (30 June 2026), now above a year of revenue. Gross trade receivables RMB90,750m at H1 FY2026, of which the three carrier-shareholders owe RMB73,385m (CMCC 40,705 / CUC 16,827 / CTC 15,853) against contractual 1-3 month terms, and RMB28.6bn is older than one year (vs 19.1bn at FY2025). ECL allowance RMB7,098m. Management attributes the H1 FY2026 OCF fall (-75% to RMB7,135m) to 'prolonged customer payment cycles and the increase in collection of receivables settled by bills'. Over FY2023-H1 FY2026 the company paid RMB27.5bn of dividends against roughly RMB12bn of owner cash (OCF - capex - leases); net debt incl. leases rose from 79.1bn to 94.7bn. The component build produces ACCRUAL owner FCF (~RMB19-20bn/yr); realised cash has been RMB15bn (FY2025), 8.8bn (FY2024), -11bn (FY2023). Treatment: (1) wc_capture_pct -60% charges steady-state working-capital intensity on revenue change in every scenario; (2) the equity_bridge deducts the PV of the near-term stretch beyond steady state (H1 FY2026 accrual not yet collected plus continued build through FY2028); (3) the bear scenario carries a permanent ~3pt EBITDA-margin haircut for ongoing leakage (unrecovered stretch and rising bad debts) and the lowest terminal cap. A dividend-discount cross-check is given in valuation_philosophy.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US, lease-heavy -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Not routed to the REIT/AFFO row: China Tower is an internally managed operator of depreciating PP&E (towers, DAS, batteries) with no IAS-40 fair-value accounting and a 25-30% capex-to-revenue intensity; the contracted-annuity character is captured in the low beta, the low WACC and the terminal cap, not by switching model. Fresh build, no prior DCF. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue RMB100,411m); 10-year explicit horizon FY2026-FY2035 because D&A and capex are still re-basing (legacy 2015-injected towers rolling off) and the FY2028 pricing-agreement reset must be inside the explicit period. SBC-zero so house and street coincide; band_position is null by construction. EBITDA margins are post-IFRS-16 reported margins (FY2025 65.5%, H1 FY2026 62.1%) with the lease charge taken separately. Cash tax 25% statutory on unlevered EBIT (FY2025 effective 24.3%, cash taxes paid RMB4,098m); the interest tax shield lives in the WACC. Capex: FY2025 RMB29,486m company basis (CSV 30,519m, cash-flow basis), H1 FY2026 11,650m (-6%), new-site build falling while Two Wings capex (RMB2,624m H1) rises. Component tie-out FY2025: EBITDA 65,814 - lease 10,506 - D&A ex-ROU 37,489 = EBIT 17,819 vs reported EBIT (PBT 15,364 + finance costs 2,446 - interest income 36) = 17,774. Buybacks: none since the RMB1.7bn of FY2019; flat count is a convention the company need not fund because SBC is zero.

bear.growth_note: Tower revenue keeps shrinking 5-7%/yr through FY2027 as the carriers consolidate sites and the H1 FY2026 rate persists; the FY2028 renewal cuts tower tariffs (-5% group), Two Wings growth slows in a weaker gig-economy/government-budget environment; flat-to-+0.5% thereafter.
bear.margin_note: 55% EBITDA margin from FY2030: ~2pt from the tariff reset and Two Wings mix, ~3pt permanent 'cash leakage' haircut representing continued receivables stretch and bad-debt write-offs by the carrier-shareholders that never unwinds (the equity_bridge only covers FY2026-28). Capex stays at 26% because site build-out is state-directed, not revenue-directed.
bear.terminal_note: 11x cap: a shrinking annuity whose cash the controlling shareholders choose when to remit; dividend-only value.

base.growth_note: FY2026 -2.0% (H1 actual -1.8%; tower -6.7% as Telecom/Unicom 'One Single Network' site consolidation and pass-through of site-fee savings bite, DAS +9%, Two Wings +14%). FY2027 -1.0% as the last year of the 2023-27 Commercial Pricing Agreement. FY2028 -2.0% for a pricing reset in the carriers' favour at renewal (the markup was cut 15%->10% in a prior cycle). FY2029 +0.5%, FY2030 +1.0%, then +1.5%: tenancy ratio ~1.8x creeping up, 5G-A densification, Two Wings reaching ~25% of revenue.
base.margin_note: Reported post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin: FY2025 65.5%, H1 FY2026 62.1% (bad-debt provisions +RMB0.5bn/yr, Two Wings mix). 62.0% FY2026, 61.5% FY2027, 60.5% from the FY2028 reset and held. Lease charge 9.8% of revenue (FY2025 10.5%, H1 FY2026 9.6%; site-fee savings). D&A ex-ROU 28% falling to 24% as fully depreciated towers roll off (H1 FY2026 run-rate 28.2%, FY2025 37.3%); capex 28% -> 25% (FY2025 29.4%, H1 FY2026 23.9%), converging on D&A for a steady-state asset base.
base.terminal_note: Cap 14x FCF: an ex-growth contracted annuity with no escalators, no pricing power over its own shareholders and a 25% capex intensity; below global tower peers (20x+ AFFO with escalators) and above the 12x used for the SOE carriers. Gordon at 6.5%/1.5% would be 20.3x, so the cap binds.

bull.growth_note: H2 FY2026 stabilises (-1.0% FY), the FY2028 renewal is price-neutral with the carriers' 5G-A and 'Six Networks' programmes adding tenants, DAS +9-10% and Two Wings +15% compound to ~2.5% group growth from FY2030.
bull.margin_note: Site-fee and power pass-through savings are partly retained, bad-debt provisioning normalises, Two Wings reaches scale: 63.5% EBITDA margin; lease charge glides to 9.0%. Receivables terms normalise (not in the bridge; see narrative).
bull.terminal_note: 16x cap: a re-rating toward a yield-asset multiple if the dividend keeps growing and payment terms normalise; still well below global tower peers.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% for the single-customer dependency (three carrier-shareholders, ~69% ownership, ~84% of revenue) combined with the live evidence that those customers are stretching payments -- RMB73bn owed against 1-3 month terms, RMB28.6bn over a year old, H1 FY2026 OCF -75%. Bull cut to 20% because it needs two independent things to go right: a price-neutral FY2028 renewal negotiated against the company's own controllers, and a normalisation of payment terms that nothing in the H1 FY2026 report suggests has begun. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
